key_terms.meaning: A crystal develops electric charge when mechanically stressed; stress → charge.
An applied voltage changes the crystal's shape; used to transmit ultrasound.
Op-amp circuit that converts tiny piezoelectric charge into a low-impedance voltage.
Measure time for a sound pulse to return; distance d = c t / 2.
Z = ρ c; a mismatch at a boundary reflects sound.
Proof mass on a spring-damper whose relative motion indicates vibration.
Seismic transducer used below resonance, with output proportional to acceleration.
V_H = R_H I B / t for a strip of thickness t.
R_H = 1/(n q) for one carrier type; its sign shows carrier type.
A magnetic material changes length when magnetized.
Stress changes the magnetization or permeability of a magnetic material.
Device that turns light into an electrical signal.
Light guided in a fibre; strain or temperature changes intensity, phase or wavelength.
Produces a pulse count; position comes from counting, and a datum is needed.
Gives a unique code for each position, so no count is lost after a power cut.
Small generator whose voltage is proportional to shaft speed.
Flashing light at adjustable frequency that freezes a rotating mark for speed measurement.
Feedback coil force cancels the input force; coil current measures force or pressure.
Electrode in a photomultiplier tube that emits secondary electrons and multiplies current.
Measures light absorbed by a sample versus wavelength to find concentration.

takeaways: Piezoelectric sensors suit dynamic force, pressure, vibration and ultrasound; a charge amplifier conditions their tiny charge.
Ultrasonic sensors use echo time or Doppler shift for distance, level and flow without touching the target.
A seismic mass on a spring and damper reads acceleration below resonance and displacement above resonance.
Hall effect sensors measure magnetic field, current or position without contact.
Magnetostrictive and magneto-elastic sensors link stress and magnetization, so they sense force, torque and position and make sound waves.
Photoelectric and fibre optic sensors convert light changes into electrical signals and allow remote or distributed measurement.
Incremental encoders count pulses, while absolute encoders give a unique code for every position.
Speed can come from a tachogenerator voltage, a stroboscope flash or a signal frequency; force-balance feedback gives high accuracy.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for construction, working principle, formula, signal conditioning, comparison and one practical application of these sensors, not just definitions.

bank.q: Explain the piezoelectric effect and the inverse piezoelectric effect. Describe a charge amplifier circuit used to condition the output of a piezoelectric pressure transducer.
outline: Crystal equivalent circuit as charge source with capacitance
Output voltage proportional to charge, not cable capacitance
Applications: dynamic pressure, vibration, ultrasound transmitter and receiver

bank.q: Describe the construction and working of a photomultiplier tube and explain how it is used with a scintillation counter.
outline: Photocathode emits electrons by photoelectric effect
Dynode chain gives secondary emission multiplication
Gain depends on number of dynodes and voltage
PMT converts light to a current pulse
Use in low-light and radiation counting

bank.q: Compare phototube, photomultiplier tube, photodiode, phototransistor, photovoltaic cell and photoconductive cell.
outline: Output type: current, voltage or resistance

bank.q: Explain the Hall effect. Derive the Hall voltage for a thin rectangular semiconductor strip and list practical applications.
outline: Charge separation creates transverse electric field
Equilibrium gives V_H = R_H I B / t
Sign of Hall voltage gives carrier type
Applications: magnetic field measurement, current sensing, proximity and position

bank.q: Explain a seismic transducer with a mass, spring and damper. Distinguish between an accelerometer and a vibrometer.
outline: Below resonance: output proportional to acceleration
Above resonance: output proportional to displacement

bank.q: Design an ultrasonic level sensor for a water tank. Explain echo timing, temperature compensation and beam selection.
outline: Transmit pulse and measure echo delay
Level from time and speed of sound

bank.q: A press needs dynamic force measurement. Compare a piezoelectric sensor with a strain-gauge load cell and recommend one with signal conditioning.
outline: Piezoelectric: charge output, dynamic, high stiffness
Strain gauge: resistive bridge, good static response

bank.q: Use an incremental encoder with quadrature output to measure the position and direction of a machine table. Explain resolution, datum and pulse counting.
outline: A and B channels in quadrature
Resolution from pulses per revolution and lead screw pitch

bank.q: Set up a fibre optic strain sensor. Explain intensity or phase modulation, source, fibre and detector choices.
outline: Strain changes fibre length or refractive index
Intensity modulation or interferometric phase modulation
Advantages: EMI immunity and remote sensing

bank.q: Measure the speed of a motor using a tachogenerator and using a stroboscope. Compare the two methods.
outline: Stroboscope freezes a mark at flash frequency
Speed from flash frequency and mark count

bank.q: Analyse the errors in an ultrasonic distance measurement caused by temperature and air movement. Compare this method with a Hall proximity sensor for position measurement.
outline: Speed of sound changes with temperature
Air currents and reflections cause error
Hall sensor needs a magnetic target and measures field change

bank.q: Evaluate piezoelectric, magnetostrictive and force-balance methods for force measurement under static and dynamic conditions.
outline: Magnetostrictive: stress changes magnetization, good for torque and force
Force-balance: feedback null, high accuracy, static and dynamic

bank.q: Evaluate the choice of photoelectric transducer for spectrophotometric concentration measurement, including dark current, noise, linearity and wavelength range.
Compare incremental and absolute encoders for a CNC axis. Discuss power failure, resolution, cost and interface.
outline: Choice for CNC safety and start-up

glossary.def: Property by which a crystal produces charge under mechanical stress and changes shape under voltage.
Circuit that converts a piezoelectric charge into a voltage while keeping input impedance high.
Device that sends and receives sound waves above 20 kHz.
Product of density and sound speed, Z = ρ c, that controls reflection at a boundary.
Proof mass mounted on a spring and damper whose motion indicates vibration.
Sensor that gives an output proportional to acceleration, often using a seismic mass.
Creation of a transverse voltage when a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field.
Material constant R_H = 1/(n q) that relates Hall voltage to current density and magnetic field.
Change of length of a magnetic material when it is magnetized.
Change of magnetization or permeability of a material when it is stressed.
Sensor that converts light intensity into an electrical current or voltage.
Thin glass or plastic strand that guides light by total internal reflection.
Position sensor that gives pulses as the shaft moves, so position is counted from a datum.
Position sensor that gives a unique digital code for each shaft position.
Small generator used to produce a voltage proportional to rotational speed.
Instrument with a flashing lamp used to freeze or measure periodic motion.
Sensor that uses feedback force to cancel an input force, so coil current measures the input.
Vacuum tube with a photocathode that emits electrons when light falls on it.
Phototube with dynodes that multiply emitted electrons to give high sensitivity.
Secondary-emission electrode inside a photomultiplier tube.
Material that emits light when ionizing radiation passes through it.
Semiconductor junction that gives a current proportional to incident light.
Bipolar transistor whose collector current is controlled by light falling on the base region.
Light-dependent resistor whose resistance falls as illumination increases.
Junction device that produces a voltage when light falls on it.
Measure of light absorbed by a sample, A = log₁₀(I₀ / I).
